newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: World airports say 1997 "off to good start".
newsitem.headline: World airports say 1997 "off to good start".

text.p: World airports reported gains in all regions in both passenger traffic and air cargo freight for January 1997, "showing the year getting off to a good start", the Airports Council International (ACI) said.

"The strongest rise was once again in air cargo freight (12.1 percent), with passenger traffic growth above the six per cent mark and total aircraft movements increasing 3.6 percent," the Geneva-based ACI said in an overnight statement.
All three averages were above the 1996 annual average, providing a "good start to 1997 for airports worldwide" it said.

Air cargo freight handled by 492 airports worldwide rose 12.1 per cent globally against January 1996, reaching 4.04 million tonnes. It was led by double-digit growth in cargo traffic in the Middle East (37 percent), Asia-Pacific (15.7 percent) and North America (12.5 percent).

"The very strong growth of cargo traffic in the Middle East shows the effectiveness of the aggressive marketing strategies of cargo hubs, such as Dubai and Sharjah," said Maria Hinayon, ACI's manager of statistics and data processing.
"In general terms, cargo traffic is also a good indicator of economic activity in its own right," she added.

Memphis, base of U.S. express freight carrier Federal Express, was the world's busiest cargo airport in January 1997 with 173,549 tonnes, up 24.2 percent over a year ago. It was followed by Los Angeles with 134,314 tonnes, up 9.9 percent.
Hong Kong ranked third at 129,917 cargo tonnes, gaining 20.3 percent, while Miami was fourth, growing just 1.5 percent.
Passenger traffic grew 6.5 per cent to 189.3 million travellers in January compared with a year ago.

The strongest passenger growth was recorded in North America (7.6 percent), the most frequently travelled region, followed closely by the Middle East (7.2 percent) and Asia-Pacific (6.1 per cent). Passenger growth was 5.5 percent in Europe.

Chicago's O'Hare airport held its position as the world's busiest passenger airport with 4.88 million travellers in January, up 4.4 percent from a year ago, followed by Atlanta with nearly 4.86 million, up 2.9 per cent.
Movement of aircrafts, landings and take-offs, rose by 3.6 percent to 3.86 million in January, boosted by a 6.1 percent jump in Europe, according to ACI.
